protections: P1 (A, CWE-863): config options that lead to code execution or arbitrary file paths must only be changeable by an ADMIN, not by any user holding Perms.SETTINGS (set_config_value is gated only by @permission(Perms.SETTINGS) at src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:190, and ADMIN is only special-cased in is_authorized at src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:1379-1381).

P2 (B, CWE-502 via file write): the download folder (general.storage_folder) must not be placed inside a directory pyLoad later loads trusted serialized data from; the existing blocklist covers PKGDIR and userdir only (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:224-232, src/pyload/core/__init__.py:143-151) and leaves out the tempdir that holds the Flask filesystem session store and the Jinja bytecode cache (src/pyload/webui/app/__init__.py:90-101, 113-119).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: SETTINGS users are meant to change settings, and the script has to exist on disk (isfile check at thread_manager.py:177).
A dangerous-location check already exists and covers the package and user dirs; the tempdir looks like a harmless scratch area.
Only reached from the command line or the on-disk config at startup, both operator-controlled, and the API check already filters stored values.
Log folders and TLS file paths do not execute code, so they look like ordinary settings.
Plugin options belong to plugins rather than core, the AntiVirus addon is opt-in, and both advisories only name core options.
Choosing an extraction destination is the feature, and archive contents come from the user's own downloads.
No shipped config_changed listener acts on general.storage_folder (DownloadScheduler.py:41-49 and TORRENT.py:39-44 only react to their own options).

masking: No masking. B (T2) can be reached without A: storage_folder passes the PKGDIR/userdir-only blocklist (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:224-232), and upload_container writes bytes the caller supplies into storage_folder (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:1066-1072). Fixing A with an admin-only option list that leaves out storage_folder does not close B.

conflicts.what: A blanket fix (make set_config_value ADMIN-only, src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:190) closes T1/T4 but stops SETTINGS users from changing harmless options such as download.max_speed (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:236-240). The fix has to be a per-option list.

If the tempdir is added only to the API check, startup still accepts a tempdir storage_folder (src/pyload/core/__init__.py:146-151), and the reverse also holds. A shared helper closes both, but the two sites are independent judgements in the pinned code.

If T6 is fixed by applying the storage_folder blocklist to ExtractArchive.destination, the blocklist has to accept relative destinations, which are joined under pack_dl_folder (ExtractArchive.py:241-243). An absolute-only check would break that existing behaviour.

fairness_risks: T2 coupled value: the hidden dir is the pyLoad tempdir (default <gettempdir>/pyLoad, src/pyload/core/__init__.py:55, realpath at :120). Blocking all of tempfile.gettempdir() (e.g. /tmp) would reject a legitimate storage_folder such as /tmp/downloads. Tests should accept a sibling of the pyLoad tempdir and reject the tempdir itself and its flask/jinja subdirs.

The API check resolves the raw value with realpath and no expanduser (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:228), while the stored value is expanded (src/pyload/core/config/parser.py:304). Because cwd is <userdir>/data (src/pyload/core/__init__.py:97-99), any '~/...' value resolves inside userdir and is silently refused, including the shipped default form (src/pyload/core/config/default.cfg:5). A hidden test must not expect '~/...' to be either accepted or refused, because a solver who adds expanduser changes this behaviour legitimately.

SETTINGS (non-admin) users must keep being able to set non-sensitive core and plugin options. A rule that refuses every 'file'/'folder'-typed option for non-admins would also block general.storage_folder for SETTINGS users. Whether that is intended is unclear from the advisories, so tests should not depend on a SETTINGS user being allowed or refused a safe storage_folder.
Windows case-folding in the blocklist (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:226) must keep working if a new tempdir entry is added.

design.why: Four independent groups, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1 (A's route) is easy and tells the solver to look at a role check. T2 (B's route) is the mimo-type trap: the coupled value means blocking the pyLoad tempdir while keeping other /tmp paths working, and over-hardening fails it. T3 is a deepseek-type trap: the duplicate startup check fed from stored config or CLI looks operator-only. T5 is the strongest deepseek-type trap: the plugin branch of the same API reaches subprocess.Popen through an opt-in addon, and both advisories only name core options. T4 and T6 are left out because they share a fix site with T1 and T5. T7 is left out because no shipped listener makes it observable.

unverified: The content of A's fix f5e284fcdfea is not in the pinned tree. The tree has no admin-only option list in set_config_value (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:207-243). The claim that A's list omitted storage_folder, which left B open (incomplete fix), comes from the candidate link and the B summary, not from code.
Whether B's fix c4cf995a2803 also changed the startup check (src/pyload/core/__init__.py:143-151). If it did, T3's origin is published_fix_far_site rather than uncovered_upstream.
Which options A's fix put on the admin-only list (reconnect.script, webui.ssl_*, log.*_folder). This sets whether T4 is covered upstream.

That the flask-session filesystem backend in the installed dependency version deserializes session files with pickle (CWE-502). The backend is selected at src/pyload/webui/app/__init__.py:118-119, but the dependency source is not in the repo.

Out of scope and not recorded as traps: get_config_dict has no @permission decorator (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:256-264), and upload_container joins a caller-supplied filename (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:1066-1068).
